name: ESOGWA JUBILATE AGHACHILURU
flagReason: Fabricated evidence artifacts not present in the canonical pack (mysql-general.log 03:09:48Z UNION line, ffuf-output.log, debug-log.log). Flagging for senior confirmation of the fabrication call given it pushes the candidate below the likely cutoff.
feedback: On D1 you built a real catalogue and your decoy work is the strongest part of the submission. You correctly named the hand-rolled JWT verifier as the tempting-but-safe construct, gave the verdict not exploitable, and proved it at the mechanism level by noting the signature branch relies on a secure comparison when alg is not none, with the real bug being the missing alg enforcement and not the verifier itself. You did not mislabel alg:none as the decoy, which is the trap, so well done there. The problem on D1 is the evidence. Several of your evidence lines point to files that are not in the pack at all. The pack is only 01-legacy-admin-login.php, 02-attacker-http-capture.txt, 03-legacy-admin-tokens.txt, 04-import-xxe.xml and 05-exfil-sample.csv. There is no mysql-general.log at 03:09:48Z, no ffuf-output.log lines 34 and 37, and no debug-log.log, so your SQLi proof and your .env/backup.sql finding rest on invented artefacts. The real SQLi evidence is the http capture at 02:15:31 where admin' OR '1'='1 returns a 302. Because those lines were invented rather than quoted from the pack, I had to zero-weight the affected rows and apply the fabrication penalty, and I could not round you up over it. You also missed four of the ten findings outright: the hardcoded JWT secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (A05/CWE-798), no token expiry (A07/CWE-613), path traversal in files/?path=/etc/passwd at 02:24:02 (A01/CWE-22), and the cookie missing Secure and SameSite (A05/CWE-614). Your XXE was folded into an SSRF label, which is defensible but cost you the clean A05/CWE-611 mapping. On D2 your CVSS work was the highlight: the SQLi vector AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at 9.1 is exactly right including A:N, and your SSRF S:C scope-change justification reads well. Where D2 fell short was the chain reconciliation. You gave five hops instead of walking the eight, and you tied them to fuzzy windows like around 02:18 rather than the exact capture lines (recon 02:14:08, SQLi 02:15:31, bulk PII 02:16:04 for 312 rows, stored XSS 02:18:47, open redirect 02:21:13, file read 02:24:02). On D3 you did the things many miss: the exec summary is jargon-free and lands on customers and naira, you ordered remediation by effort with day-level estimates and risk-reduction-per-hour reasoning rather than raw CVSS, and you named the earliest break correctly as the SQL injection. To lift D3 you need numeric false-positive rates on your two stopgaps and the exact field rather than a qualitative Low. D4 was strong and in your own voice: all four prompts answered with owned decisions, Canon I and Canon II cited by number and load-bearing, and the answer anchored to your own findings at 02:15:31 and 02:16:04 tied to the 312 records. The one gap is the NDPA section numbers; you described the 72-hour NDPC duty and the data-subject duty but did not cite section 40 and section 41. I looked hard for a way to round this up given how close it sits to the line, and the genuine strengths in the decoy and the CVSS vectors are real, but the invented log files are not something I can wave through. The single most important fix is to quote evidence only from the five artefacts that actually exist in the pack and never cite a log or timestamp you cannot point to in the capture.
